mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen for three consecutive weeks (-19.0 to -17.7). This momentum reflects a self-reinforcing recovery in shopping and leisure activity as households adapt routines, and should continue to push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks absent a new shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC rose each of the last three weeks from -19.0 to -17.7
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean is lower than its trailing 4-week mean despite three prior weeks of consecutive improvement, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops sharply week-on-week (a proxy for new restriction announcements such as London entering a higher COVID tier), commuting and non-essential travel curtail, which within two weeks drags RETAIL_REC downward as footfall to shops and venues falls.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has been near -28 to -30 for four weeks, close to prior restriction-era lows
failure_condition: If a TRANSIT drop exceeding 5 points is observed but RETAIL_REC's subsequent 2-week mean does not decline relative to the prior 2-week mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The joint rebound of PARKS (-14.9 to -12.6) alongside persistently high RESIDENTIAL (~14.6-15.3) suggests households are substituting outdoor recreation for retail errands during a transitional period, so when PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, RETAIL_REC growth is dampened in the very short term as outdoor activity substitutes for shopping trips.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS jumped from -16.0 to -12.6 while RESIDENTIAL stayed flat near 14.6-15.3
failure_condition: If PARKS continues rising together with stable high RESIDENTIAL but RETAIL_REC's next 1-week mean rises rather than falls relative to the current week, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: As the UK approaches the late-October clock change and shortening daylight, outdoor park visits (PARKS) are expected to decline seasonally, shifting discretionary activity indoors and increasing RETAIL_REC over the following four weeks as shopping substitutes for outdoor leisure.
candidate_trigger: calendar date crosses the late-October clock change (daylight saving end)
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2020-10-15 is within two weeks of the UK's daylight saving end on 2020-10-25
failure_condition: If PARKS declines seasonally after the clock change but RETAIL_REC's 4-week forward mean does not rise relative to its trailing 4-week mean, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a Tier 2-style restriction regime where WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain persistently suppressed (around -15 and -28 respectively), limits on indoor hospitality and household mixing structurally cap RETAIL_REC recovery, keeping its forward 2-week mean lower than it would be in an unrestricted regime.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES has stayed between -15.6 and -17.1 and TRANSIT between -28.0 and -30.3 for four weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain in their current suppressed bands but RETAIL_REC's forward 2-week mean rises above its trailing 2-week mean, the regime-suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -15 points (a sign of modestly increased office attendance), the associated weekday commuter footfall will lift nearby retail and food-service visits, raising RETAIL_REC within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -17.1 to -15.6 over the last three weeks
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES crosses above -15 but RETAIL_REC's following 1-week mean does not increase relative to the current week, the commuter-footfall hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained growth in GROCERY_PHARM mobility (from -2.0 to +2.3 over four weeks) indicates households are consolidating errands into essential-only trips, a behavioral pattern that structurally limits discretionary RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM rose steadily from -2.0 to 2.3 across the four weeks
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM continues rising but RETAIL_REC's forward 4-week mean also rises relative to its trailing 4-week mean, the essential-trip substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Joint stagnation of TRANSIT and WORKPLACES at depressed levels combined with persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL indicates an entrenched work-from-home equilibrium; this combination interacts to suppress any near-term rebound in RETAIL_REC because reduced commuting flows remove incidental retail visits.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT near -28 to -30, WORKPLACES near -15 to -17, RESIDENTIAL near 14.6-15.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: If TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and RESIDENTIAL all remain in their current stagnant bands but RETAIL_REC's forward 2-week mean rises relative to its trailing 2-week mean, the joint-stagnation interaction hypothesis is rejected.
